title: Cheapest Card Grading (2026)
verdict: The cheapest card grading in 2026 by sticker price is GMA at $9 to $12 a card and CGC bulk at $10, and AGS is the cheapest way to get a measured grade with subgrades, at $15 to $18.

On sticker price alone AGS is not the cheapest. GMA lists $12 a card with a 25-card minimum and $9 at 100, and CGC's bulk tier is $10 with a 10-card minimum on cards worth up to $500. Beckett's Base tier is $14.95 if you can wait 45 business days or more. Pick those when the lowest number is the only thing that matters.

why: There is no value upcharge. A $20 card and a $20,000 card cost the same $18 to grade at AGS, and bulk orders of 30 or more start at $15. Subgrades and the report are included, where Beckett charges $3 more for subgrades at its Base tier.

Bulk pricing starts at 30 cards, a low bar for a dealer. TCG cards are $15 each at 20 business days, $20 at 10 and $30 at 5, and sports cards are $3 more per tier. Every card in a bulk order still gets the full report and eight subgrades.

The wait is short because the grading step is short. AGS lists 20 business days or less on its standard service, 10 and 5 business days on the faster tiers, and same-day grading on request for urgent cards.

faq.q: What is the cheapest card grading?
faq.a: GMA at $12 a card with a 25-card minimum, or $9 at 100 cards. CGC's bulk tier is $10 from 10 cards worth up to $500 each. For a single card, Beckett's Base tier is $14.95 and AGS is $18.

faq.q: How many cards count as a bulk order?
faq.a: 30 at AGS. CGC's bulk tier starts at 10 cards, GMA's economy tier at 25, and GMA drops its price again at 100.

faq.q: How much does AGS charge to grade a card?
faq.a: $18 per card at the standard rate, whatever the card is worth. Bulk orders of 30 or more TCG cards are $15 each at 20 business days, $20 at 10 or $30 at 5. Sports and non-TCG bulk is $3 more per tier.

faq.q: Is there a minimum number of cards?
faq.a: Not at AGS. You can send one card at $18, and bulk pricing needs 30. CGC's bulk tier needs 10 cards, ISA needs 10, and GMA needs 10 to 25 depending on the tier.

faq.q: Is it worth grading a low-value card?
faq.a: Only if grading lifts the price by more than the fee plus shipping, or if you want the card protected and documented. At $10 to $18 a card the math works on far more cards than at $50.
